title: Jar candles, pillars and event tealights: measured, not guessed

say: Jar candles, pillars and event tealights: measured, not guessed.
This is the video for module 2 of Candle Making: Container, Pillar and Small Candle Production.
Most candle businesses sell three families. Jar candles are the best first product: the jar holds the wax, the candle cannot fall over, and customers love them as gifts.

say: For example, Halima in Kaduna has 12 identical jars. First she does a test pour, because every jar is different.

panel.heading: Halima's batch of 12 jars
items: Test pour: full 390 g minus empty 210 g = 180 g
Add 5 percent for loss: 2,268 g of wax
Fragrance at 6 percent: about 136 g

say: The empty jar weighs 210 g. Filled with set wax to the line, it weighs 390 g. So one jar holds 180 g of wax.

say: For 12 jars, that is 12 times 180, which is 2,160 g.

say: Some wax always stays on the jug and spoon, so she adds about 5 percent. 2,160 times 1.05 gives 2,268 g to melt.

say: Fragrance load means fragrance oil as a percentage of the wax weight. She chooses 6 percent, so 2,268 times 0.06 gives about 136 g of oil.

say: Never go above your supplier's maximum. Extra oil can leak out, which is called sweating, and can make the candle burn unsafely.

panel.rule: Never go above the fragrance maximum on your data sheet.

say: Wash and dry the jars, then fix a pre-tabbed wick in the centre of each one.

panel.heading: Pouring the jar candles
items: Fix and centre a wick in each clean jar
Warm the jars slightly, not in water
Melt wax to the data sheet temperature
Add dye, then fragrance at its temperature
Pour slowly to the fill line
Cool without draughts; top up and cure

say: Warm the jars slightly in a warm place. Cold glass can make wax pull away from the sides.

say: Now pillars.
The bottom of the mould becomes the top of the candle.
To know how much wax to melt, fill the sealed mould with water and weigh it.
Wax is lighter than water, so the same grams of wax will be enough.

panel.heading: Pillars: shrinkage is part of the method

cards.d: Fill the sealed mould with water and weigh it. Melt that many grams of wax: it is enough.
Keep some wax back. When a firm skin forms, poke relief holes near the wick.
Fill the dip with the reserved wax. Unmould only when fully cool. Never force it.

say: For example, Ruth in Jos melts 400 g of pillar wax and keeps about 60 g back. When a firm skin forms on the first pour, she pokes two or three relief holes near the wick to let trapped air out.

panel.heading: Pillars: shrinkage is part of the method

cards.d: Fill the sealed mould with water and weigh it. Melt that many grams of wax: it is enough.
Keep some wax back. When a firm skin forms, poke relief holes near the wick.
Fill the dip with the reserved wax. Unmould only when fully cool. Never force it.

say: As it shrinks, a dip forms. She reheats the reserved wax and fills it. That is the second pour, not a repair. She waits until it is completely cool, and it slides out easily.

say: A tealight is poured into its own small cup and burns inside it, so you can make them fast in rows on a tray.
For example, Grace in Benin City needs 48 tealights.
Each cup holds 14 g, so she melts about 706 g, and makes 50 so she can burn test two before delivery.
A votive melts into a pool of liquid wax, so it must burn in a holder only slightly larger than the candle. Tell customers clearly, or hot wax will spread across the table.
Before you accept an event order, ask in writing: how many, what colour and scent, the delivery date and address, and whether the venue allows open flames.
Agree the price and deposit in the same message.
And keep dried flowers, paper, ribbons and glitter out of the wax the flame will reach. Decorate the jar, lid or box instead.

panel.heading: Event orders and decoration safety
items: How many, colour and scent, in writing
Delivery date and address
Does the venue allow open flames?
Price and deposit agreed in the same message
Flowers, ribbon, glitter: outside only

say: To remember. Test pour first. Multiply, then add about 5 percent. Keep fragrance within the maximum. Give every pillar relief holes and a second pour. And votives always burn in a holder.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A test pour gives the true wax weight
Wax per jar x jars, plus about 5 percent
Fragrance never above the supplier's maximum
Pillars: relief holes and a second pour
Votives always burn in a holder
